narrativeProgression.description: The woman begins reading the title, author, and publication details of the scientific article.
A webpage displaying an illustration of two merging black holes appears on the screen.
The woman starts reading the article, describing the discovery of two intertwined supermassive black holes.
The narrative details the use of NASA's Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE) in the discovery.
Further observations made with the Australian Telescope Compact Array and the Gemini South telescope in Chile are mentioned.
The narrative shifts to discussing the WISE satellite's mission and its recent reactivation for asteroid hunting.
The focus returns to the black hole binary discovery, explaining the initial misinterpretation of data and the eventual realization of the binary nature of the system.
The discussion expands to the general nature of supermassive black holes and their growth through galactic cannibalism and mergers.
The narrative returns to the specifics of the newly discovered black hole binary and its significance as a relatively rare observation of a merging event in its early stages.
The role of radio images from the Australian Telescope Compact Array in identifying the dual nature of the system is highlighted.
The text describes the unusual zigzag pattern observed in the jets emanating from the black holes and the hypothesis about the influence of one black hole on the other's jet.
The final stages of merging black holes and their implications for gravitational waves are briefly discussed.
The scene ends with details about the institutions involved in the WISE mission and the scientific study.
